title: Video to GIF Shortcut Not Working? Fixes and Alternatives
description: The Video to GIF shortcut fails or makes huge files? Check photo access, iCloud downloads, clip length and the large-data setting, or use a GIF app instead.
h1: Video to GIF shortcut not working: fixes and alternatives
card_title: Video to GIF shortcut not working
card_summary: Why the Shortcuts GIF maker fails on long or iCloud videos, and what to do.
quick_answer: Most failures come from four things: Shortcuts has no access to Photos (Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > Shortcuts), the video is still in iCloud and needs to download first, the clip is too long for the shortcut to process, or Shortcuts blocks large data (Settings > Apps > Shortcuts > Advanced > Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data). Trim the video shorter and try again; if you need control over size and quality, use a dedicated GIF app.
intro: The Video to GIF shortcut from Apple's Shortcuts Gallery is a great free tool, but it runs every frame through a simple pipeline with no settings, so long or high-resolution clips can fail silently, take ages or produce enormous files.
Here are the fixes, in order of how often they help.

screenshot.alt: Creating GIF progress at 34 percent with a Cancel button in Make Video to GIF
screenshot.caption: A dedicated app shows progress and lets you cancel long exports.

sections.heading: Fixes
paragraphs: Try these one at a time:
list: Give Shortcuts photo access: Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > Shortcuts > Full Access.
Download the video first: open it in Photos and wait until it plays without a loading circle.
Trim a long video in Photos (Edit) before running the shortcut, or pick a shorter clip.
Allow large data: Settings > Apps > Shortcuts > Advanced > Allow Sharing Large Amounts of Data.
Remove the shortcut and add it again from the Gallery if you edited its actions.
Restart the iPhone if Shortcuts stops responding; low free storage can also make it fail.

sections.heading: When the shortcut works but the GIF is bad
paragraphs: Huge files, choppy motion or the wrong framing are not bugs: the shortcut has no frame rate, crop or size controls unless you edit its actions. An app with those settings fixes this without building your own shortcut.

steps.heading: Alternative: make the GIF in Make Video to GIF
steps.intro: Same clip, with settings and progress.

items.name: Open the video
items.text: Pick it in Make Video to GIF, or share it from Photos into the app.

items.name: Trim
items.text: Tap Edit Video and keep the seconds you need.

items.name: Adjust
items.text: Set FPS, crop and loop in GIF settings and check the estimated size.

items.name: Convert
items.text: Tap Convert to GIF; a progress ring shows how far along it is, and you can cancel.

items.name: Share or save
items.text: Send it from the share sheet or save it to Photos.

tips.heading: Tips
items: 4K or 60 FPS videos are the most likely to fail in the shortcut; trim them first.
If the shortcut saves a GIF that won't move, see the guide on GIFs not working on iPhone.
Keep both: the shortcut for quick throwaway GIFs, an app when size and quality matter.

faq.question: Why does the Video to GIF shortcut do nothing?
faq.answer: Usually missing photo access or a video that is still downloading from iCloud. Check both, then try a short clip.

faq.question: Why is the shortcut's GIF so big?
faq.answer: It keeps the full resolution and frame rate. Trim the clip shorter or use an app that lets you lower FPS and crop.

faq.question: Is there a better free alternative?
faq.answer: The Make GIF shortcut handles Live Photos and bursts. For videos with size control, use a dedicated GIF app.
